Shake-to-undo marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Shake to Undo workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Shake to Undo vs in-app Undo vs swipe-to-undo

US pages use "Shake to Undo", "Shake to undo typing", or "Undo last edit." China storefront copy often uses 摇动撤销 for Apple's Accessibility feature name, 摇一摇撤销 when pointing to the shake gesture itself, or 摇动手机撤销输入 for shake-to-undo typing marketing — depending on whether you mean system Shake to Undo, in-app undo demos paired with shake, or text-entry recovery workflows. Shake to Undo vs Reachability vs AssistiveTouch

Shake to Undo (摇动撤销) triggers undo when the user physically shakes the device. Reachability (便捷访问) pulls the screen down for one-handed reach. AssistiveTouch (辅助触控) shows a floating on-screen menu. Do not reuse Reachability or AssistiveTouch framing on Shake to Undo toggle frames unless that is what the screenshot depicts.

Text-entry apps vs general productivity marketing

Shake to Undo marketing often pairs with Notes, Mail, Messages, Pages, journaling, or custom text-editor badges. zh-Hans copy should name text-entry workflows only when your English listing and screenshots already claim them — not imply universal shake undo on every screen when your gallery shows typing-specific art.

Accidental-shake settings vs disable-when-not-needed framing

Some apps market accidental-shake false-positive settings or guidance to disable Shake to Undo when not needed. Match caption vocabulary to the surface your gallery actually markets; generic shake-undo copy does not belong on unrelated feature frames.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement Shake to Undo APIs or motion-detection code?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. Shake to Undo OS integration, motion detection, undo-stack rendering, and Settings deep-link engineering are outside scope.

How is Shake to Undo listing copy different from Reachability, AssistiveTouch, or Touch Accommodations?

Shake to Undo listing copy covers undo triggered by physically shaking the device — under Settings → Accessibility → Shake to Undo. Reachability covers bringing the top of the screen down for one-handed reach. AssistiveTouch covers the on-screen floating assistive menu. Touch Accommodations covers hold duration and tap-assistance settings. Those are different buyer stories with different screenshot vocabulary.

How is Shake to Undo different from in-app Undo buttons or swipe-to-undo on the product page?

Shake to Undo is a system accessibility setting triggered by shaking the device. In-app Undo toolbar buttons or swipe-to-undo gestures are separate UX surfaces. If your English listing mentions both, zh-Hans copy should name each workflow accurately per screenshot frame.

How is this different from Voice Control, Hover Text, or Zoom?

Voice Control covers spoken device commands. Hover Text covers enlarged text near the pointer when hovering. Zoom covers whole-screen magnification. Shake to Undo covers shake-gesture undo for typing and edits — a different framing on the product page.
